usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/image-resize?image_url=<URL>&target_width=<int>&target_height=<int>&format=png&fit=cover (all params are query string; all optional but image_url + target dims needed for a useful result)
usage.outputShape: body.base64 (resized image, base64-encoded), body.width, body.height, body.format, body.size_bytes, body.content_type; metadata at body._meta.payment
quirks: All inputs are QUERY-STRING params on a GET (no JSON body): image_url, target_width, target_height, format (png|jpeg|webp), fit (cover|contain|fill|inside|outside), quality.

CHARGES EVEN ON FAILURE: a source image the server cannot fetch returns HTTP 400 'Failed to fetch image' but STILL bills ~$0.0324. Use a reliably server-fetchable image URL (a Wikipedia upload.wikimedia.org URL was rejected with 400; httpbin.org/image/png worked).
Output image is returned as base64 string in body.base64, not a binary body.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.strale.io/x402/image-resize with query params: image_url (URL-encoded, must be a publicly+server-fetchable image), target_width, target_height, plus optional format (png/jpeg/webp) and fit (cover/contain/fill/inside/outside). It pays via x402 (~$0.032/call on Base) and returns JSON synchronously. Read the resized image from body.base64 (decode it), with body.width/height/format/size_bytes describing the result. Important: pick an image URL you know the server can fetch — bad/blocked URLs return HTTP 400 but you are still charged.
